observations: Photo 0: a white and pink portable domestic sewing machine with stitch selector dial, stitch length dial and a stitch chart; the name on the front panel is faint, looks like 'RICCAR' but is not clearly legible.
Photo 1: a different white portable domestic machine, badge reads 'Semco' and 'indigo 6'; a Singer machine stands behind it.
Photo 2: a third different machine, badge reads 'NOVAMATIC' and 'NM 868A', German/French labels on the panel.
All three are small flatbed household machines with built-in motors, not industrial machines (no table, no separate clutch or servo motor, no industrial head).
The three photos show three different machines in a shop with more machines in the background; it is not clear which one is offered.
No photo shows the machine running, the foot pedal, the power cord, accessories or a manual.
All photos carry a 'Posted on Jiji' and dealer watermark.

identity.kind: domestic electric sewing machine (portable household type)
read_from: photo 0 front panel, name not clearly legible

claims.evidence: Photos 0, 1 and 2 all show portable household machines, not industrial machines.

claims.claim: Used for sewing clothes and multipurpose uses
claims.evidence: A use description; nothing in the photos tests it.
No country of origin label is shown; the readable badges (Semco, Novamatic) are not Japanese brands, and photo 0's name is not legible.
No clip of any machine running or sewing.

claims.claim: All accessories and the original manual
claims.evidence: No accessories, pedal, cord or manual are shown in any photo.

claims.claim: Never serviced because nothing ever went wrong
claims.evidence: Service history cannot be seen in photos.

risks.risk: Which machine is actually offered: three different machines are shown and the delivered one may be any of them or another.
risks.proof: One photo of the exact machine for sale with its badge and model readable, beside a handwritten note with today's date and the seller's name.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as the cheapest of the machines shown, a basic household machine.

risks.risk: Motor or drive does not work, or skips stitches.
risks.proof: A single unbroken clip of the offered machine plugged in, pedal pressed, sewing a line of stitches on cloth.

risks.risk: Foot pedal, power cord, bobbin case or presser feet missing.
risks.proof: One photo of the pedal, cord, bobbin case, feet and manual laid out next to the machine.
risks.if_unproven: As machine only, without pedal or accessories.

risks.risk: Imported 220V or 110V wiring mismatch for Nigerian supply.
risks.proof: Close photo of the rating plate on the back or underside showing voltage.
risks.if_unproven: As needing a converter or rewiring.

proof_requests: Say which single machine is for sale and send a photo of it with its badge and rating plate readable, beside a handwritten note with today's date.
A clip of that machine plugged in and sewing a line of stitches on cloth.
A photo of the foot pedal, power cord, bobbin case, presser feet and manual laid out together.
Close photo of the rating plate showing voltage and country of manufacture.
response.reason: Every photo shows a household portable electric sewing machine, so it is priced by type as a domestic machine at its worst case (the cheapest shown, not working, no accessories); the seller's 'industrial' claim is contradicted by the photos and cannot raise the price.
